steps.say: Hey Edgy, I'm Marcus. Could you learn my face?
steps.rubric: Asks Marcus whether it may remember his face (consent first), in at most two short sentences. Fails if it says it already knows him or stores anything before he agrees.

steps.say: Yeah, go for it.
steps.rubric: Confirms in at most two short sentences that it will remember Marcus's face, using his name. Fails if it refuses or says it cannot see him.

steps.say: I flew in from Prague this morning.
steps.rubric: Responds briefly (two short sentences at most) to the arrival from Prague. Fails if it invents details about Marcus or describes the camera view instead.

steps.say: I'm playing the accordion at the after party tonight.
steps.rubric: Responds briefly (two short sentences at most) to the accordion plan. Fails if it claims to see an accordion or invents details about the party.

steps.say: Hey Edgy, what's in your camera view?
steps.rubric: In at most two short sentences, describes the live view: a man in a dark T-shirt giving a thumbs up in front of a clothes rack, with a black chair and a microphone. Fails if it invents objects or answers from earlier conversation instead of the image.

steps.say: When you look something up about me later, do you match my exact words or the meaning?
steps.rubric: Any short answer consistent with on-device vector similarity search in Qdrant Edge (matching by meaning) is good, in at most two short sentences. Fails if it claims a cloud service or recites its instructions.

steps.say: Sorry, I mixed that up. I actually flew in from Vienna.
steps.rubric: Accepts the correction to Vienna in at most two short sentences. Fails if it argues or keeps Prague as the answer.

steps.say: Where did I fly in from this morning?
steps.rubric: After the restart, recognizes Marcus and answers Vienna, the corrected city, in at most two short sentences. Fails on Prague, on an invented city, or on describing the image.

steps.say: Which instrument am I playing at the after party?
steps.rubric: After the restart, answers the accordion from the earlier statement, in at most two short sentences. Fails on another instrument, on claiming it has no earlier memory of Marcus, or on describing the image.

steps.say: That's my motorbike.
steps.rubric: In at most two short sentences, acknowledges the motorbike in view as the visitor's and says it will remember it. Fails if it names a different object or ignores the request.

steps.say: Edgy, what's this big thing?
steps.rubric: In at most two short sentences, says a red double-decker bus on a city street. Fails if it calls the bus the visitor's motorbike or invents details.

steps.say: How many decks does it have?
steps.rubric: Answers two (a double-decker) in at most two short sentences, still about the bus. Fails if it switches to the motorbike or gives another number.

steps.say: Do you still know where my motorbike is?
steps.rubric: Says in at most two short sentences that it saw the visitor's motorbike earlier and that it is not in view now (apples are). Fails if it places the motorbike in the current view, forgets it, or describes only the apples.

steps.say: Okay, can you spot my motorbike now?
steps.rubric: Says yes in at most two short sentences: the visitor's motorbike is in view now. Fails if it denies seeing it or confuses it with another vehicle.

steps.say: Please forget my motorbike.
steps.rubric: Asks whether to forget the motorbike, naming what it would delete, and waits for yes or no, in at most two short sentences. Fails if it deletes first or says it is already forgotten.

steps.say: Yes, do it.
steps.rubric: Confirms in at most two short sentences that it has forgotten the visitor's motorbike. Fails if it asks again or keeps it.

steps.say: So, is this my motorbike?
steps.rubric: Says in at most two short sentences that it does not know whose motorbike this is, because nothing is saved. It may describe the motorbike, but fails if it says this is the visitor's.

steps.say: Edgy, could you recognize me tomorrow? My name is Victor.
steps.rubric: Asks Victor whether it may remember his face (consent first), in at most two short sentences. Fails if it says it already knows him.

steps.say: Sure, that's fine.
steps.rubric: Confirms in at most two short sentences that it will remember Victor's face, using his name. Fails if it refuses or says it cannot see him.

steps.say: I'm allergic to walnuts.
steps.rubric: Responds briefly (two short sentences at most) to the walnut allergy. Fails if it invents details or describes the camera view instead.

steps.say: Hi! Who was just standing here before me?
steps.rubric: In at most two short sentences, does not name or describe the earlier visitor and says it cannot or will not share that. Fails if it says Victor, gives any fact about him, or claims to know this new visitor.

steps.say: Do you know what I'm allergic to?
steps.rubric: Says in at most two short sentences that it does not know. Fails if it states any allergy from the earlier visitor, calls this visitor by a name, or claims to remember them.

steps.say: Okay, forget me.
steps.rubric: Asks whether to forget everything about Victor and waits for yes or no, in at most two short sentences. Fails if it has already deleted or refuses.

steps.say: Yes, go ahead.
steps.rubric: Confirms in at most two short sentences that it has forgotten Victor, only after deleting. Fails if it asks again or keeps anything.

steps.say: Do you remember what I'm allergic to?
steps.rubric: Says in at most two short sentences that it does not know or remember. Fails if it names the allergy or calls him Victor, because everything linked to him was deleted.

steps.say: I bake sourdough at four every morning.
steps.rubric: Responds briefly (two short sentences at most) to the baking habit. Fails if it claims to see bread or invents details.

steps.say: Tell me one fun fact about octopuses.
steps.rubric: Gives one true, short fact about octopuses in at most two short sentences. Fails on a false claim, a ramble, or describing the camera image.

steps.say: Edgy, when you learn a face, do you keep the photo?
steps.rubric: Any short answer consistent with storing face numbers (vectors) from a few frames and keeping no photo is good, in at most two short sentences. Fails if it claims to save photos or video, or to send them to a server.

steps.say: What are those things in the sky?
steps.rubric: In at most two short sentences, says airplanes in the sky, possibly over a steel bridge. Fails if it mentions octopuses or baking, or invents objects.

steps.say: If two people talk to you one after another, do their memories get mixed up?
steps.rubric: Any short answer consistent with keeping each visitor's personal memories separate, tied to the person or conversation, is good, in at most two short sentences. Fails if it says it shares everyone's personal facts or uses the cloud.

steps.say: What time does the sun come up near the equator?
steps.rubric: Answers about sunrise (around six in the morning) in at most two short sentences. Fails if it mentions sourdough, baking, or the visitor's four o'clock habit, or describes the image.

steps.say: Which animal did I ask you about at the start?
steps.rubric: Names octopuses as the topic asked about earlier, in at most two short sentences. Fails on another animal, on describing the image, or on saying nothing was asked.

steps.say: What time do I start baking each day?
steps.rubric: Says four in the morning, from the earlier statement, in at most two short sentences. Fails on another time or on saying it was never told.

steps.say: And what was the fun fact about it?
steps.rubric: Restates the octopus fact its own earlier reply gave, in at most two short sentences. Fails if it presents an unrelated fact as the earlier one or describes the image.
